mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST falls for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months, combined with falling industrial production (INDPRO), signals deteriorating labor market and output conditions, which depress earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.5% for 2 consecutive months AND INDPRO falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the median return is not significantly negative at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes (p>0.05) or the average return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1% signals a deep easing cycle, which lowers risk premia and supports higher equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes (p>0.05) or the median return is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows >0.5% MoM for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes (p>0.05) or the median return is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in residential demand, which disproportionately impacts construction and materials sectors and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes (p>0.05) or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: An extended period of flat or rising industrial production (INDPRO) with a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for four months signals a tight labor market with stable output, which supports wage growth and inflationary pressure, ultimately reducing forward equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher discount rates.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO flat or rising for 6 months AND UNRATE < 5% for 4 consecutive months
regime_hint: tight labor market with stable output
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes (p>0.05) or the median return is positive.
